Absent brain structures and cranial vault are defining neurologic and skeletal malformations. Adrenal hypoplasia at 30-79% supports metabolic_endocrine involvement.
Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy defines neurologic disease. The ancestry and gene do not establish an independent metabolic disorder.
The tumour occupies the brainstem. Its vascular appearance and hemangioma ancestry do not establish cardiovascular disease; hemangioblastoma stromal cells are the neoplastic component.
A radial nerve lesion directly affects the peripheral nervous system. Neuritis ancestry alone does not establish an infectious or immune-mediated cause.

Cardiomyopathy, renal disease and mitochondrial metabolism define the disorder. Cerebral atrophy and developmental impairment occur in 30-79%; additional myopathy is appropriately acknowledged beyond the cap.
Musculoskeletal reasonably represents the defining mesenchymal soft-tissue neoplasm. Renal and pulmonary origins belong to particular subtypes and cannot be assigned universally to this umbrella.
Defining eosinophilia and immune-mediated myofascial disease support the primary axes. Persistent skin thickening occurs in 30-79%; other qualifying organs are acknowledged beyond the cap.

Add metabolic_endocrine: inherited failure of surfactant catabolism is a defining metabolic disorder. Pulmonary disease and intrinsic alveolar macrophage dysfunction support the existing primary axes.

corrected.basis: Inherited GM-CSF receptor dysfunction impairs macrophage surfactant catabolism, causing intraalveolar phospholipid accumulation and respiratory dysfunction.
